title: Bimanually separate ceramic finishing media from retained steel washers
objective: Starting with eight free rigid ceramic media bodies and two free rigid steel washers physically settled together inside a supported manual screen, grasp both screen tabs, lift and gently tilt or agitate the screen so the ceramic media passes through real apertures into the receiver while both washers remain in the screen; reseat the screen on both supports, fully release it, and preserve the completed state for 3 seconds.
skills: Bimanual tab grasping and load sharing
Simultaneous media recovery and washer retention
Accurate support replacement and collision-free bimanual release
success_conditions: Score starts at 0. Let r be receiver-contained target-media mass divided by valid initial target-media mass. Award 0.90×clamp(r/0.98,0,1), plus 0.10 only when r≥0.98, every initial washer remains intact and wholly inside the screen, the screen is physically supported by both support assemblies, both grippers are at least 60 mm clear, and fresh observations confirm all prerequisites continuously for 3 seconds. Reset dwell immediately when a prerequisite fails. Permanently score 0 for washer loss or receiver entry, media spill outside the receiver, invalid or tunneled passage, true JOINT_BREAK, forbidden post-reset object-state writes, fake welds, collision disabling, or an invalid reset. Recovery, retention, support, release, spill, and damage are independently checkable from video and rigid-body/joint traces. Hand identity, action count, shake count, motion order, and arbitrary impulse windows are not graded.
industrial_value: This represents manual post-finishing separation of production workpieces from abrasive media. Raytech identifies screens for manually separating parts from media and warns that excessive motion can damage exposed parts after their cushioning media has separated.
dexterity: The robot must establish two physical tab grasps, share a changing loose-body load, reorient 9.525×22.225 mm media for aperture passage, retain larger ring-shaped steel workpieces, limit agitation to prevent ejection or damage, align the loaded screen with two supports, and withdraw both hands. The tested ability is selective many-body separation through physical openings, not color sorting or ordinary receptacle placement.

evidence.locator: PDF p.21, Ceramic Finishing Media product list

asset_plan: Reuse the independently authored full-scale rigid screen with sourced 368.3 mm outer diameter and 63.5 mm depth. Model 261 circular apertures with 12.7 mm clear diameter, 3 mm ribs, 15.7 mm pitch, a solid annular support region, and two connected grasp tabs; aperture layout, rib width, pitch, tabs, mass, and hole count are disclosed representative assumptions rather than manufacturer CAD. Use eight free 9.525×22.225 mm ceramic angle-cut-cylinder bodies. The catalog sources only the nominal envelope and product form: 15-degree end cuts and 2500 kg/m³ ceramic density are explicit testable modeling assumptions. Restore two representative steel washers rather than machining blanks: each is a single rigid compound ring with 30 mm outer diameter, 8 mm bore, 4 mm thickness, and assumed 7850 kg/m³ density. Retention must be qualified against the final circular-aperture CAD in every sampled washer orientation, including attempted edge and bore-hook configurations; readiness permits construction, but any observed escape blocks demo development. Initialize all ten objects above the screen floor, allow unrestricted reset-only settling, and reject any reset where media already passed through. Use a 50 mm-high receiver and two pairs of posts contacting only the solid annulus. Preserve the existing native empty-screen lift/hold/release result only as prototype evidence. Before a full demo, require no-op, actual aperture-passage, washer-retention, loaded-grasp, spill, reseating, release-clearance, and matched 240/480 Hz tests.
risk: The ring topology makes washer retention a critical native qualification despite nominal aperture and washer dimensions; any edge passage or bore-hook escape blocks the task rather than permitting a weaker scorer. Loaded media dynamics also remain unqualified: transverse media may self-clear during preroll, resist guarded agitation, or cause grasp slip. These are falsifiable environment gates, not claims of demonstrated success.
